reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer, controlled aerobic runs that are crucial for building the endurance necessary for trail racing, while Plan B focuses almost exclusively on very short, easy runs. The inclusion of two longer runs (86 and 100 minutes) in Plan A directly addresses the need for sustained effort, a key component of trail running performance. Furthermore, Plan A includes a more balanced approach to recovery with only one dedicated rest day, allowing for better adaptation to the training load.
